title: Tenant-aware fast-fallback procedure for canary regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Create and validate a tenant-aware, low-latency fallback and communication procedure that can be executed across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments when a canary introduces a regression. Goal is to reduce customer‑facing error windows to <10 minutes for critical tenants and provide a repeatable playbook that ties engineering mitigation steps with customer communications and SRE runbook actions.

Background: Recent canary deployments surfaced regressions that only affected a subset of tenants due to model variant routing + tenant pinning logic and KV cache inconsistencies. Existing rollbacks are cross-env and slow when tenant-specific pinning or private control planes are involved. This ticket captures a formalized fast-fallback flow, verification signals, and communication templates for coordinated customer escalations and hotfix paths.
acceptance_criteria: A documented runbook exists that runs through fast-fallback (tenant pin -> route swap -> cache invalidate) with time-to-swap measured in staging < 5 minutes
Automated circuit-breaker flags (metric + signal) are defined per-tenant and wired to paging for oncall
Customer communication templates (p0/p1) are in Confluence and approved by Support & PM
A smoke verification suite (canary smoke) runs post-swap and returns green for top-20 tenants within 10 minutes
Rollback can be executed in Hosted, Dedicated, and Private environments with a single documented checklist and owner mapping
steps_taken: Scoped the failure modes with SRE and Applied ML — identified tenant-pin mismatch and stale KV cache as primary vectors (2026-03-09)
Validated that Dedicated control planes require tenant-aware RPC to perform pin swaps — created prototype RPC in runtime-agent (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1823)
Implemented metric tags for tenant_id on error-rate, latency-p50/p90, and model-variant-fallbacks in prometheus (merged 2026-03-10)
Drafted initial Confluence runbook for review: /confluence/display/RUN/Fast+Fallback+Playbook (draft v1)
Ran tabletop with SRE, Support, and PM to iterate communication flow — captured contact matrix for Dedicated and Private customers
next_steps: Finalize and publish Confluence runbook (owner: Liam) and route to Support for approval (due 2026-03-14)
Add automated tenant circuit-breaker alerting rule for hosted-prod (owner: SRE team) and verify alert noise < 2/day
Ship runtime-agent endpoint to perform tenant-pin swap in private control plane (PR 1823 -> merge -> canary)
Add smoke job in CI that validates top-20 tenants after a swap (owner: QA) and expose result in rollout dashboard
Prepare customer-facing templates for Status page, targeted emails, and CSM scripts; attach to runbook

runbook_checklist: Notify SRE oncall and create incident bridge
Identify affected tenant IDs and their deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
Set tenant circuit-breaker for affected tenants to bypass canary variant
Trigger tenant-pin swap via runtime-agent (or manual override for Private)
Invalidate KV cache for affected tenant(s) and confirm cache miss metrics
Run smoke checks for top-20 tenant flows and confirm no increase in error-rate
Inform customer via targeted template and update status page
Monitor for 30 minutes, if unstable, coordinate model rollback and engage PM/CSM
